title: Exact structure, required fields
statement: Give the writer the item's exact structure and make every field that matters required; without a structure items failed far more often, and fields left optional got left out.
example: With no schema, the pass rate fell to 5% against a 45% baseline.
detail: In the same prompt sweep, raw generation with no schema passed 5% of items against a 45% baseline, at 20 items per variant (`icloud-work/ML learnings/prompt_engineering_deep_dive.md`). One writer filled every schema field, optional ones included, while another often left optional fields out, such as the source attribution, so the anchor-fact field was made required (`icloud-work/ML learnings/week_of_apr_21.md`). Any structural deviation fails an item on specification compliance (`icloud-work/ML learnings/what_is_ap_and_why_it_matters.md`).
against: Structure doesn't carry correctness: "The knowledge and content quality within the structure is what differentiates model sizes — not the structural compliance itself" (`icloud-work/ML learnings/research_model_size_vs_data_quality.md`, line 150). In the same sweep factual accuracy moved much less than the pass rate (50% with no schema against 60% at baseline), and structure is a hard fail only for some item types (`icloud-work/ML learnings/evaluation_methodology.md`, lines 44-50).

evidence.quote: Gemini reliably fills all JSON schema fields including optional ones. Fireworks model frequently omits optional fields (e.g., `source_attribution`). Keep required fields minimal; never rely on optional field presence for correctness. The `anchor_fact` field is required in the schema specifically because of this.
Any structural deviation = automatic fail on `specification_compliance`.
Reply with JSON only, matching the shape you are given exactly.
